title: 細胞工学
subtitle: Cell Engineering
educationalGoal: Biology and technology are harnessed to serve many purposes including: (1) gene therapies, (2) drug therapies, biologics, (3) food production and biofuel development, (4) understanding the breadth of biotechnology and how it can serve as a research tool.
advice: This course is designed to acquaint a non-scientist professional with aspects of science as they apply to the biotechnology industry. Biology and technology are harnessed to serve many purposes including gene therapies, drug therapies, biologics, food production and biofuel development. Grasping the breadth of biotechnology can be confusing to a student. This is because modern-day research not only studies biological problems in a classical sense, but also puts biological principles to work as research tools. Antibodies are an example of a fundamental component of the immune system, yet antibodies are also used as tools by researchers to detect other proteins and are being developed in ways to work like drugs to treat diseases such as cancer. In a wider sense, the inner workings of cells are examined to identify defects in diseases, yet cells are also used to make products like biofuels. This course is specifically designed to give an overview of the biotech industry and to teach the scientific principles that apply to numerous biotechnology sectors.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology. Students should have learned basic cell biology.
